61	# sysup uv-tool-python: pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor
62	
63	Source: discovered 2026-10-24 from a sysup run failure. `uv tool upgrade --all` tried to resolve `mempalace` against CPython 3.15 (the newest uv-managed interpreter after a Homebrew `python@3.15` landed), where `onnxruntime` (a transitive dep via `chromadb`) has no `cp315` wheel, so the whole resolution was unsatisfiable and the uv step failed. The immediate drift was fixed by hand (`uv tool install --python 3.14 --force mempalace`, receipt now records `python = "3.14"`), but nothing in sysup prevents recurrence for `mempalace` or any other freestanding uv tool.
64	
65	## Overview
66	
67	### Problem Statement
68	sysup keeps mise `pipx:` tools on a known-good python minor through the `pipx-python` capability (`src/tools/sysup/capabilities/pipx_python.py`, wired at `order: 65` in `default.yaml`): it reads each `--managed-python --python X.Y` pin, moves any stale one to the global mise python minor, reinstalls, and reverts a tool that fails to build on the new minor.
69	
70	Freestanding `uv tool` installs get no such guard. The uv step is just `[uv, python, upgrade]` then `[uv, tool, upgrade, --all]` (`default.yaml:36-37`). `uv tool upgrade` resolves each tool against the interpreter recorded in its receipt (`~/.local/share/uv/tools/<tool>/uv-receipt.toml`); a tool installed without `--python` has no `python` key in the receipt and re-resolves against the newest uv-managed interpreter available. When a new CPython minor lands (here 3.15 via Homebrew) before the native-wheel ecosystem catches up, an unpinned tool with a compiled transitive dep (`onnxruntime`, `tokenizers`, ...) becomes unsatisfiable, and `uv tool upgrade --all` fails for the whole batch.
71	
72	The host currently has three freestanding uv tools (`uv tool list`: `engram`, `huggingface-hub`, `mempalace`); `mempalace` and `engram` both pull compiled deps, so this is not a one-tool accident.
73	
74	This PRD adds a sysup capability that, before `uv tool upgrade --all` runs, pins every freestanding uv tool whose receipt has no `python` key (or a stale minor) to the global mise python minor and reinstalls it, reverting any tool that fails to build on that minor to its prior interpreter — the exact safety contract `pipx-python` gives mise tools.
75	
76	### Target Users
77	The solo operator running `sysup` by hand or from a scheduler, whose uv-tool upgrades must survive a new CPython minor landing before compiled wheels exist for it.

86	## Functional Decomposition
87	
88	### Capability: Pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor
89	Before the uv upgrade step re-resolves them, every freestanding `uv tool` is anchored to a python minor the mise global already uses, so an upgrade never drifts to an interpreter without wheels.
90	
91	#### Feature: Discover installed uv tools and their recorded python
92	- **Description**: Enumerate the tools under the uv tools directory and read the interpreter each receipt pins (if any).
93	- **Inputs**: the uv tools dir (`uv tool dir` output, fallback `$XDG_DATA_HOME/uv/tools` then `~/.local/share/uv/tools`); each tool's `uv-receipt.toml`.
94	- **Outputs**: a list of `(tool_name, pinned_minor_or_none)`.
95	- **Behavior**: `uv tool dir` gives the root; each immediate subdirectory is a tool. The receipt's `[tool]` table may hold a `python` key (a version or minor string, e.g. `"3.14"`); its minor (`^(\d+\.\d+)`) is the pinned minor, `None` when the key is absent. Tools are read-only here; nothing is written during discovery. Parsing uses `tomllib` (stdlib, 3.11+), already the project baseline.
96	
97	#### Feature: Move each tool onto the global minor
98	- **Description**: A tool with no pin, or a pin below the global mise python minor, is reinstalled pinned to that minor; a tool already on it is left alone.
99	- **Inputs**: the discovered `(tool, pinned)` list, the global mise python minor (`mise current python` run from `$HOME`, minor only), the resolved `uv` and `mise` binaries.
100	- **Outputs**: one `StepResult` per tool actually moved (`<tool> (python <old> -> <target>)`, `old` is the prior minor or `unpinned`); a single `ok` result `all uv tools on python <target>` when nothing needs moving.
101	- **Behavior**: mirrors `PipxPython`. `uv python install <target>` once up front; then for each stale tool `uv tool install --python <target> --force <tool>`. On success, the receipt now records the target. On failure, reinstall at the prior interpreter — `uv tool install --python <old> --force <tool>` when it had a pin, else `uv tool install --force <tool>` (no `--python`, restoring the unpinned state) — and report the step failed with `kept on python <old>` / `kept unpinned` plus the captured stderr, so one bad wheel never leaves a tool broken. A tool already on the target minor is skipped (no reinstall call).
102	- **Guards**: `uv` or `mise` missing -> one `ok`-framed skip result `uv or mise not found, skipping` (not a failure, matching `pipx-python`'s "skipping" wording is `success=False`; re-decided here as `success=False` to stay identical to the sibling). No global mise python minor -> `success=False`, `no global mise python version, skipping`. No tools at all -> one `ok` result `no uv tools installed`.
103	
104	#### Feature: Wire the capability before the uv upgrade
105	- **Description**: A `default.yaml` entry runs this capability before `uv tool upgrade --all` re-resolves the tools.
106	- **Inputs**: the command table in `src/tools/sysup/default.yaml`.
107	- **Outputs**: a new `uv-tool-python` command entry.
108	- **Behavior**: the `uv` entry (`order: 40`) runs `[uv, python, upgrade]` then `[uv, tool, upgrade, --all]`. The new entry must pin BEFORE that upgrade, so it either (a) becomes `order: 35` running ahead of `uv`, or (b) the `uv` entry's steps are split so pinning sits between `uv python upgrade` and `uv tool upgrade --all`. Decided at create-prd: option (a) — a separate `uv-tool-python` entry at `order: 35`, `when: { os: darwin, check: uv }`, `use: uv-tool-python` — keeps the capability independently skippable and testable and leaves the `uv` entry's two-step shape untouched. `uv python upgrade` (patch-level bumps of already-installed minors) at `order: 40` does not install new minors, so running the pin at 35 against the current global minor is correct; the pin targets the mise global minor, not whatever `uv python upgrade` might touch.

263	If the root has no candidate tools, yield exactly one successful result with message `no uv tools installed`. On nonzero exit or `OSError`, attempt rollback for that tool: `[uv, "tool", "install", "--python", old, "--force", tool]` when previously pinned, or `[uv, "tool", "install", "--force", tool]` when previously unpinned. # sysup uv-tool-python: pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor

Source: discovered 2026-10-24 from a sysup run failure. `uv tool upgrade --all` tried to resolve `mempalace` against CPython 3.15 (the newest uv-managed interpreter after a Homebrew `python@3.15` landed), where `onnxruntime` (a transitive dep via `chromadb`) has no `cp315` wheel, so the whole resolution was unsatisfiable and the uv step failed. The immediate drift was fixed by hand (`uv tool install --python 3.14 --force mempalace`, receipt now records `python = "3.14"`), but nothing in sysup prevents recurrence for `mempalace` or any other freestanding uv tool.

## Overview

### Problem Statement
sysup keeps mise `pipx:` tools on a known-good python minor through the `pipx-python` capability (`src/tools/sysup/capabilities/pipx_python.py`, wired at `order: 65` in `default.yaml`): it reads each `--managed-python --python X.Y` pin, moves any stale one to the global mise python minor, reinstalls, and reverts a tool that fails to build on the new minor.

Freestanding `uv tool` installs get no such guard. The uv step is just `[uv, python, upgrade]` then `[uv, tool, upgrade, --all]` (`default.yaml:36-37`). `uv tool upgrade` resolves each tool against the interpreter recorded in its receipt (`~/.local/share/uv/tools/<tool>/uv-receipt.toml`); a tool installed without `--python` has no `python` key in the receipt and re-resolves against the newest uv-managed interpreter available. When a new CPython minor lands (here 3.15 via Homebrew) before the native-wheel ecosystem catches up, an unpinned tool with a compiled transitive dep (`onnxruntime`, `tokenizers`, ...) becomes unsatisfiable, and `uv tool upgrade --all` fails for the whole batch.

The host currently has three freestanding uv tools (`uv tool list`: `engram`, `huggingface-hub`, `mempalace`); `mempalace` and `engram` both pull compiled deps, so this is not a one-tool accident.

This PRD adds a sysup capability that, before `uv tool upgrade --all` runs, pins every freestanding uv tool whose receipt has no `python` key (or a stale minor) to the global mise python minor and reinstalls it, reverting any tool that fails to build on that minor to its prior interpreter — the exact safety contract `pipx-python` gives mise tools.

### Target Users
The solo operator running `sysup` by hand or from a scheduler, whose uv-tool upgrades must survive a new CPython minor landing before compiled wheels exist for it.

## Functional Decomposition

### Capability: Pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor
Before the uv upgrade step re-resolves them, every freestanding `uv tool` is anchored to a python minor the mise global already uses, so an upgrade never drifts to an interpreter without wheels.

#### Feature: Discover installed uv tools and their recorded python
- **Description**: Enumerate the tools under the uv tools directory and read the interpreter each receipt pins (if any).
- **Inputs**: the uv tools dir (`uv tool dir` output, fallback `$XDG_DATA_HOME/uv/tools` then `~/.local/share/uv/tools`); each tool's `uv-receipt.toml`.
- **Outputs**: a list of `(tool_name, pinned_minor_or_none)`.
- **Behavior**: `uv tool dir` gives the root; each immediate subdirectory is a tool. The receipt's `[tool]` table may hold a `python` key (a version or minor string, e.g. `"3.14"`); its minor (`^(\d+\.\d+)`) is the pinned minor, `None` when the key is absent. Tools are read-only here; nothing is written during discovery. Parsing uses `tomllib` (stdlib, 3.11+), already the project baseline.

#### Feature: Move each tool onto the global minor
- **Description**: A tool with no pin, or a pin below the global mise python minor, is reinstalled pinned to that minor; a tool already on it is left alone.
- **Inputs**: the discovered `(tool, pinned)` list, the global mise python minor (`mise current python` run from `$HOME`, minor only), the resolved `uv` and `mise` binaries.
- **Outputs**: one `StepResult` per tool actually moved (`<tool> (python <old> -> <target>)`, `old` is the prior minor or `unpinned`); a single `ok` result `all uv tools on python <target>` when nothing needs moving.
- **Behavior**: mirrors `PipxPython`. `uv python install <target>` once up front; then for each stale tool `uv tool install --python <target> --force <tool>`. On success, the receipt now records the target. On failure, reinstall at the prior interpreter — `uv tool install --python <old> --force <tool>` when it had a pin, else `uv tool install --force <tool>` (no `--python`, restoring the unpinned state) — and report the step failed with `kept on python <old>` / `kept unpinned` plus the captured stderr, so one bad wheel never leaves a tool broken. A tool already on the target minor is skipped (no reinstall call).
- **Guards**: `uv` or `mise` missing -> one `ok`-framed skip result `uv or mise not found, skipping` (not a failure, matching `pipx-python`'s "skipping" wording is `success=False`; re-decided here as `success=False` to stay identical to the sibling). No global mise python minor -> `success=False`, `no global mise python version, skipping`. No tools at all -> one `ok` result `no uv tools installed`.

#### Feature: Wire the capability before the uv upgrade
- **Description**: A `default.yaml` entry runs this capability before `uv tool upgrade --all` re-resolves the tools.
- **Inputs**: the command table in `src/tools/sysup/default.yaml`.
- **Outputs**: a new `uv-tool-python` command entry.
- **Behavior**: the `uv` entry (`order: 40`) runs `[uv, python, upgrade]` then `[uv, tool, upgrade, --all]`. The new entry must pin BEFORE that upgrade, so it either (a) becomes `order: 35` running ahead of `uv`, or (b) the `uv` entry's steps are split so pinning sits between `uv python upgrade` and `uv tool upgrade --all`. Decided at create-prd: option (a) — a separate `uv-tool-python` entry at `order: 35`, `when: { os: darwin, check: uv }`, `use: uv-tool-python` — keeps the capability independently skippable and testable and leaves the `uv` entry's two-step shape untouched. `uv python upgrade` (patch-level bumps of already-installed minors) at `order: 40` does not install new minors, so running the pin at 35 against the current global minor is correct; the pin targets the mise global minor, not whatever `uv python upgrade` might touch.

## Test Strategy

### Critical Scenarios
- **Happy path**: one unpinned tool (receipt has no `python` key), global minor 3.14 -> Expected: `uv python install 3.14` once, `uv tool install --python 3.14 --force <tool>`, one `(python unpinned -> 3.14)` success result.
- **Happy path**: a tool pinned to 3.13, global 3.14 -> Expected: moved, `(python 3.13 -> 3.14)`.
- **Edge case**: a tool already pinned to 3.14, global 3.14 -> Expected: no reinstall call for it; the run yields `all uv tools on python 3.14` when it is the only tool.
- **Edge case**: no tools under the uv tools dir -> Expected: one `no uv tools installed` result, no install calls.
- **Error case**: a tool fails to build on 3.14 -> Expected: a second `uv tool install` reverting it to its prior interpreter (or unpinned), a `success=False` result with `kept on python <old>` / `kept unpinned` and the stderr; other tools still processed.
- **Error case**: `mise current python` empty -> Expected: `success=False`, `no global mise python version, skipping`, no install calls, no filesystem change.
- **Error case**: `uv` or `mise` not on PATH -> Expected: a single skip result, nothing run.

## Risks

- **A tool genuinely needs the newest minor** and has no wheel on the global minor either: the revert path keeps it on its prior interpreter and reports failure (amber-visible via the attention layer); it is not silently downgraded past a working state. Accepted — the operator sees the failed step and can pin that one tool by hand.
- **`uv tool dir` output or receipt schema changes across uv versions**: mitigated by the `$XDG_DATA_HOME`/`~/.local/share/uv/tools` fallback for the dir and by treating a missing `[tool].python` key as unpinned; a receipt that fails to parse is treated as unpinned (so the tool is re-pinned, the safe direction) rather than crashing the run.
- **Ordering vs `uv python upgrade`**: the pin runs at `order: 35`, before both `uv python upgrade` and `uv tool upgrade --all` (`order: 40`). `uv python upgrade` only bumps patch levels of installed minors, so it cannot introduce the newer minor that caused the drift; the pin targets the mise global minor regardless. Mitigated by the `test_default_config` ordering assertion.
- **Divergence from `pipx-python`**: two capabilities now enforce "global python minor" with near-identical logic. Accepted — they act on different tool systems (mise config pins vs uv receipts) and share no mutable state; factoring a common helper is out of scope here and would couple two independently-evolving capabilities.

```python
def _tool_dir(uv: str) -> Path: ...
def _global_minor(mise: str) -> str | None: ...
def _pinned_minor(receipt_path: Path) -> str | None: ...

class UvToolPython:
    @property
    def inputs(self: UvToolPython) -> Mapping[str, object]: ...

    def run(self: UvToolPython, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]: ...

    def _move(
        self: UvToolPython, uv: str, tool: str, old: str | None, target: str
    ) -> StepResult: ...
```

`_tool_dir` runs `[uv, "tool", "dir"]` with captured text and `check=False`. Use a successful nonempty stripped path; otherwise use nonempty `$XDG_DATA_HOME/uv/tools`, otherwise `Path.home() / ".local/share/uv/tools"`. Do not create the directory. A missing root is empty; a root that exists but cannot be listed yields a failed discovery result, not a false no-tools success. Enumerate sorted immediate subdirectories only; ignore files and dot-prefixed metadata directories. Resolve receipt names from directory names without invoking a shell.

`_pinned_minor` reads `uv-receipt.toml` with `tomllib`, requires a `[tool]` table, and returns the leading `X.Y` from a supported numeric version string. An absent `python` key alone returns `None`. Compare minor tuples `(int(major), int(minor))`, never strings: move an absent pin or one below the target; leave equal and newer pins untouched. This follows the PRD's “below the global” predicate rather than copying the sibling's `!=` predicate, which could downgrade a deliberate newer pin.

Safety preflight is part of `_pinned_minor`, before any reinstall. A bare-name reinstall is supported only for a receipt whose original request is that same normalized package name with no customization: `requirements` is exactly `[tool_name]` in the legacy string form or `[{"name": tool_name}]` in uv's structured form; normalize names by lowercasing and collapsing `[-_.]+` to `-`. Explicitly empty `extras` and empty `specifier` in that single structured requirement are also harmless. `constraints`, `overrides`, `excludes`, and `build-constraint-dependencies` must be absent or empty; `options` must be absent or `{}`. Allow uv-owned `entrypoints` metadata but reject an entrypoint with a nonempty `from` naming a different package. Unknown substantive keys in `[tool]` or the requirement object are unsupported. These checks ensure the PRD's bare `<tool>` argv cannot discard an original source, extras, dependency injection, index, constraint, or resolver option.

Missing/malformed receipts, a missing requirements identity, unsupported customizations, and a present `python` that is not a numeric version are distinguishable failures, never silently treated as an unpinned plain package. Catch `OSError`, `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`, and validation `ValueError` per tool, yield `StepResult(tool, success=False, message="<reason>, skipping")`, and continue other tools. Numeric selectors match `\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?` with an optional prerelease suffix; selectors such as `pypy@3.10`, `cpython@3.14`, paths, executable names, ranges, and free-threaded `3.14t` remain untouched with an explicit unsupported-selector failure. Do not add selector resolution or a general receipt-to-argv translator in this PRD.

This is a deliberate safety refinement of the PRD's malformed-receipt fallback: without readable installation intent, a bare package reinstall cannot guarantee recovery. It changes no acceptance criterion or named scenario; it reports the unsupported case visibly instead of claiming that parsing failure proves an ordinary unpinned install.

If the root has no candidate tools, yield exactly one successful result with message `no uv tools installed`. If all safely read pins equal the target, yield exactly one successful result with message `all uv tools on python <target>`. If there are only equal/newer pins and at least one newer pin, use the truthful message `all uv tools pinned to python <target> or newer`. Never emit an all-current success when any receipt was skipped with failure. When there are eligible moves, run `[uv, "python", "install", target]` once before the first move. If it fails, yield one failed result containing `uv python install <target> failed: <stderr-or-unknown error>` and stop without tool installs.

`_move` returns one `StepResult` labelled `<tool> (python <old-or-unpinned> -> <target>)`. Its initial argv is exactly `[uv, "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", tool]`. On exit zero, return success. On nonzero exit or `OSError`, attempt rollback for that tool: `[uv, "tool", "install", "--python", old, "--force", tool]` when previously pinned, or `[uv, "tool", "install", "--force", tool]` when previously unpinned. All installs capture text and use `check=False`. Do not edit receipts directly; uv owns its environment and receipt writes. Continue processing later tools after either outcome.

Only a zero rollback exit permits `kept on python <old>` or `kept unpinned` in the failed result. A failed rollback reports `reinstall on python <old> also failed` or `unpinned reinstall also failed`, including both initial and rollback diagnostics. Never claim a working tool after failed recovery. Use `stderr.strip()` with `unknown error` fallback for nonzero commands. An `OSError` supplies its exception text. Unpinned rollback restores absence of an explicit request, not necessarily the identical historical interpreter; no stronger recovery claim is made. Recovery of exact package versions, or an environment snapshot, is outside this PRD's contract.

The registry addition is exactly `"uv-tool-python": UvToolPython()`. Preserve the registry module's current `__all__` public surface. Add this bundled command entry:

```yaml
  # Pin freestanding uv tools to the global python minor before uv tool upgrade.
  uv-tool-python:
    order: 35
    when: { os: darwin, check: uv }
    use: uv-tool-python
```

Keep `uv.order == 40` and its steps exactly `(("uv", "python", "upgrade"), ("uv", "tool", "upgrade", "--all"))`. Before implementation, recheck that premise; if it changed, stop and report as the PRD requires. No command dependency or fail-fast policy is added: this capability reports failed tools while the existing runner continues its normal plan.

103	    """Move plain uv tool installations to the global mise Python minor."""

105	    @property
106	    def inputs(self: UvToolPython) -> Mapping[str, object]:
107	        return {}

109	    def run(self: UvToolPython, **_kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]:
110	        uv, mise = shutil.which("uv"), shutil.which("mise")
111	        label = "uv tool python"
112	        if uv is None or mise is None:
113	            yield StepResult(label, success=False, message="uv or mise not found, skipping")
114	            return
115	        try:
116	            target = _global_minor(mise)
117	            if target is None:
118	                yield StepResult(label, success=False, message="no global mise python version, skipping")
119	                return
120	            root = _tool_dir(uv)
121	            try:
122	                tools = sorted(path for path in root.iterdir() if not path.name.startswith(".") and path.is_dir())
123	            except FileNotFoundError:
124	                tools = []
125	        except OSError as exc:
126	            yield StepResult(label, success=False, message=str(exc))
127	            return
128	        if not tools:
129	            yield StepResult(label, success=True, message="no uv tools installed")
130	            return
131	
132	        moves: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
133	        skipped = newer = False
134	        target_version = tuple(map(int, target.split(".")))
135	        for directory in tools:
136	            try:
137	                old = _pinned_minor(directory / "uv-receipt.toml")
138	            except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
139	                skipped = True
140	                yield StepResult(directory.name, success=False, message=f"{exc}, skipping")
141	                continue
142	            version = tuple(map(int, old.split("."))) if old is not None else None
143	            if version is None or version < target_version:
144	                moves.append((directory.name, old))
145	            newer |= version is not None and version > target_version
146	        if not moves:
147	            if not skipped:
148	                message = (
149	                    f"all uv tools pinned to python {target} or newer" if newer else f"all uv tools on python {target}"
150	                )
151	                yield StepResult(label, success=True, message=message)
152	            return
153	        error = _install_error([uv, "python", "install", target])
154	        if error is not None:
155	            yield StepResult(label, success=False, message=f"uv python install {target} failed: {error}")
156	            return
157	        for tool, old in moves:
158	            yield self._move(uv, tool, old, target)

160	    def _move(self: UvToolPython, uv: str, tool: str, old: str | None, target: str) -> StepResult:
161	        label = f"{tool} (python {old or 'unpinned'} -> {target})"
162	        error = _install_error([uv, "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", tool])
163	        if error is None:
164	            return StepResult(label, success=True)
165	        rollback = [uv, "tool", "install"]
166	        if old is not None:

168	        recovery = _install_error([*rollback, "--force", tool])
169	        if recovery is None:

171	        else:
172	            state = f"reinstall on python {old} also failed" if old else "unpinned reinstall also failed"
173	            state = f"{state}: {recovery}"
174	        return StepResult(label, success=False, message=f"{state}: {error}")

    @staticmethod
    def _receipt(root, tool, *, python=None, requirement=None, extra=""):
        directory = root / tool
        directory.mkdir(parents=True)
        requirement = requirement or f'["{tool}"]'
        text = f"[tool]\nrequirements = {requirement}\n"
        if python is not None:
            text += f'python = "{python}"\n'
        path = directory / "uv-receipt.toml"
        path.write_text(text + extra)
        return path

    @staticmethod
    def _fake_run(mocker, root, *, current="3.14.6\n", current_code=0, directory_code=0, directory=None, outcomes=None):
        pending = {tuple(argv): list(values) for argv, values in (outcomes or {}).items()}

        def run(argv, **kwargs):
            assert isinstance(argv, list)
            assert kwargs.get("capture_output") is True
            assert kwargs.get("text") is True
            assert kwargs.get("check") is False
            assert not kwargs.get("shell", False)
            if argv == ["/bin/mise", "current", "python"]:
                assert kwargs.get("cwd") == Path.home()
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, current_code, current, "")
            if argv == ["/bin/uv", "tool", "dir"]:
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                    argv, directory_code, str(root) if directory is None else directory, ""
                )
            assert argv[:3] in (["/bin/uv", "python", "install"], ["/bin/uv", "tool", "install"])
            result = pending.get(tuple(argv), [(0, "")]).pop(0)
            if isinstance(result, OSError):
                raise result
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, result[0], "", result[1])

        mocker.patch("sysup.capabilities.uv_tool_python.shutil.which", side_effect=lambda name: f"/bin/{name}")
        return mocker.patch("sysup.capabilities.uv_tool_python.subprocess.run", autospec=True, side_effect=run)

    @staticmethod
    def _installs(mock_run):
        return [call.args[0] for call in mock_run.call_args_list if call.args[0][1:3] == ["tool", "install"]]

    def test_pins_unpinned_tool_to_global_minor_and_reinstalls(self, mocker, tmp_path, target, structured) -> None:

        first = self._receipt(root, "gita", requirement=requirements)
        second = self._receipt(root, "gita-extra")
        originals = [first.read_bytes(), second.read_bytes()]
        mock_run = self._fake_run(mocker, root, current=f"{target}.8\n")

        steps = list(UvToolPython().run())

        assert [(step.label, step.success) for step in steps] == [
            (f"gita (python unpinned -> {target})", True),
            (f"gita-extra (python unpinned -> {target})", True),
        ]
        installs = [
            ["/bin/uv", "tool", "install", "--python", target, "--force", tool] for tool in ("gita", "gita-extra")
        ]
        assert self._installs(mock_run) == installs
        calls = [call.args[0] for call in mock_run.call_args_list]
        interpreter = ["/bin/uv", "python", "install", target]
        assert calls.count(interpreter) == 1
        assert calls.index(interpreter) < calls.index(installs[0])

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from buvis.pybase.filesystem.atomic_write import atomic_write_text

from sysup.step_result import StepResult

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping

__all__ = ["PipxPython"]

_DEFAULT_CONFIG = "~/.config/mise/config.toml"
_PIN = re.compile(r'^"(pipx:[^"]+)" = .*--managed-python --python (\d+\.\d+)', re.MULTILINE)
_MINOR = re.compile(r"^(\d+\.\d+)")


def _set_pin(path: Path, tool: str, version: str) -> None:
    pattern = re.compile(rf'^("{re.escape(tool)}" = .*--managed-python --python )\d+\.\d+', re.MULTILINE)
    atomic_write_text(path, pattern.sub(rf"\g<1>{version}", path.read_text(), count=1))


class PipxPython:
    """Move mise pipx tools pinned to uv-managed python onto the global mise python minor.

    Only entries whose ``uvx_args`` carry ``--managed-python --python X.Y`` are
    touched. Each stale pin is rewritten in the mise config and the tool is
    reinstalled; a tool that fails to install on the new minor is reverted to
    its old pin and reinstalled there, so one bad wheel never leaves it broken.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: PipxPython) -> Mapping[str, object]:
        return {"config": _DEFAULT_CONFIG}

    def run(self: PipxPython, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]:
        mise, uv = shutil.which("mise"), shutil.which("uv")
        if mise is None or uv is None:
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message="mise or uv not found, skipping")
            return

        path = Path(str(kwargs.get("config", _DEFAULT_CONFIG))).expanduser()
        if not path.is_file():
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message=f"{path} not found, skipping")
            return

        target = self._global_minor(mise)
        if target is None:
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message="no global mise python version, skipping")
            return

        stale = [(m.group(1), m.group(2)) for m in _PIN.finditer(path.read_text()) if m.group(2) != target]
        if not stale:
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=True, message=f"all pinned pipx tools on python {target}")
            return

        install = subprocess.run([uv, "python", "install", target], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        if install.returncode != 0:
            message = install.stderr.strip() or "unknown error"
            yield StepResult("pipx python", success=False, message=f"uv python install {target} failed: {message}")
            return

        for tool, old in stale:
            yield self._move(mise, path, tool, old, target)

    def _global_minor(self: PipxPython, mise: str) -> str | None:
        # Run from $HOME so a project-local python pin can't redefine the target.
        result = subprocess.run(
            [mise, "current", "python"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
            cwd=Path.home(),
        )
        match = _MINOR.match(result.stdout.strip()) if result.returncode == 0 else None
        return match.group(1) if match else None

    def _move(self: PipxPython, mise: str, path: Path, tool: str, old: str, target: str) -> StepResult:
        label = f"{tool} (python {old} -> {target})"
        _set_pin(path, tool, target)
        result = subprocess.run([mise, "install", "-f", tool], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return StepResult(label, success=True)

        message = result.stderr.strip() or "unknown error"
        _set_pin(path, tool, old)
        restore = subprocess.run([mise, "install", "-f", tool], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        state = f"kept on python {old}" if restore.returncode == 0 else f"reinstall on python {old} also failed"
        return StepResult(label, success=False, message=f"{state}: {message}")

"""Run the unchanged suite in writable isolated host state/config, report runner counts."""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

environment = dict(os.environ)
environment.update(
    UV_CACHE_DIR='/tmp/gems-autocodex-uv-cache',
    XDG_STATE_HOME='/tmp/gems-autocodex-test-state',
    BUVIS_CONFIG_DIR='/tmp/gems-autocodex-test-config',
)
result = subprocess.run(
    ['uv', 'run', '--no-sync', 'pytest', '-q', '--tb=line'],
    env=environment, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=600,
)
sys.stdout.write(result.stdout)
summary = next((line for line in reversed(result.stdout.splitlines()) if re.search(r'\d+ (?:passed|failed)', line)), '')
counts = {kind: int(value) for value, kind in re.findall(r'(\d+) (passed|failed|skipped)', summary)}
if not counts:
    raise SystemExit(result.returncode or 2)
print(f'PASS {counts.get("passed", 0)} FAIL {counts.get("failed", 0)} SKIP {counts.get("skipped", 0)} EXIT {result.returncode}')
raise SystemExit(result.returncode)

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from sysup.capabilities.gh_token import GhTokenExpiry
from sysup.capabilities.helm import HelmRepoUpdate
from sysup.capabilities.nvim_mason import NvimMason
from sysup.capabilities.pip import PipOutdated
from sysup.capabilities.pipx_python import PipxPython
from sysup.capabilities.sudo import SudoPrime
from sysup.capabilities.uv_tool_python import UvToolPython
from sysup.capabilities.x509 import X509Expiry

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
    from datetime import datetime

    from sysup.step_result import StepResult

__all__ = [
    "CAPABILITIES",
    "EXPIRY_CAPABILITIES",
    "Capability",
    "ExpiryCapability",
    "GhTokenExpiry",
    "X509Expiry",
]


@runtime_checkable
class Capability(Protocol):
    """A built-in, code-owned updater referenced from config by name.

    ``inputs`` declares the accepted ``with:`` keys mapped to their default
    values, so ``load_config`` can reject unknown inputs. ``run`` executes the
    capability and yields one :class:`StepResult` per reported step. A capability
    may raise :class:`buvis.pybase.result.FatalError` for an unrecoverable
    precondition (e.g. a missing required binary); any other exception is caught
    by the runner and turned into a failed step.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: Capability) -> Mapping[str, object]: ...

    def run(self: Capability, **kwargs: object) -> Iterator[StepResult]: ...


CAPABILITIES: dict[str, Capability] = {
    "helm-repo-update": HelmRepoUpdate(),
    "nvim-mason": NvimMason(),
    "pip-outdated": PipOutdated(),
    "pipx-python": PipxPython(),
    "sudo-prime": SudoPrime(),
    "uv-tool-python": UvToolPython(),
}


@runtime_checkable
class ExpiryCapability(Protocol):
    """A built-in, code-owned expiry probe referenced from config by name.

    ``inputs`` declares the accepted ``with:`` keys mapped to their default
    values, so ``load_config`` can reject unknown inputs; a default of ``None``
    marks a key the config validator treats as required on an enabled item.
    ``expires_at`` returns an aware :class:`datetime.datetime` when the expiry is
    known, or a :class:`str` naming why it is unknown. A probe may raise
    :class:`buvis.pybase.result.FatalError` for an unrecoverable precondition;
    any other exception is caught by the runner and reported as unknown.
    """

    @property
    def inputs(self: ExpiryCapability) -> Mapping[str, object]: ...

    def expires_at(self: ExpiryCapability, **kwargs: object) -> datetime | str: ...


EXPIRY_CAPABILITIES: dict[str, ExpiryCapability] = {
    "gh-token-expiry": GhTokenExpiry(),
    "x509-expiry": X509Expiry(),
}
